newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber closes mixed after setting new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber closes mixed after setting new highs.

text.p: CME lumber futures ran up to new contract highs in May and July early before correcting in an overbought market, traders said.

Profit taking developed when cash trade remained slow. Cash prices were up somewhat as warmer weather improved building conditions and suggested lumber demand would revive. But trade remained slow and prices were not up as much as expected. Futures held a large premium to cash after rallying sharply last week, tradrs said.
Futures closed $0.90 per tbf lower to $6.50 higher with March up $1.80 at $427.30 and May off $0.20 at $395.30. May and July had posted new contract highs early.

Expectations of increased demand for lumber as warmer weather spreads across the country added to carryover buy stops to boost futures prices early. ING was an early buyer with Refco selling on the early advance, they added.
Futures closed at noon CST in observance of the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday.
